items.description: Navigating the stock-filing route via <App> renders the stock-filing form page
The stock-filing form contains an input carrying data-testid="sku-input"
The stock-filing form contains an input carrying data-testid="location-input"
The stock-filing form contains an input carrying data-testid="quantity-input"
The stock-filing form contains an input carrying data-testid="inventory-code-input"
The stock-filing form contains a submit button carrying data-testid="submit-stock"
Filling all fields and submitting the stock-filing form calls the JSON API with SKU, location, quantity, and inventory_code
After a successful API response the form shows a confirmation element carrying data-testid="file-success-message"
The stock boundary module (app/routes/) contains no import of the database Session object
The stock boundary module (app/routes/) contains no import of any SQLAlchemy ORM model class
The stock service module (app/services/) contains no import of any SQLAlchemy ORM construct or Session
The database connection string is read from an environment variable and is not hardcoded anywhere in the source tree
The stock service raises a validation error for a write where quantity is less than zero before any database call is issued
Inserting a stock record with sku set to NULL is rejected by the database
Inserting a stock record with location set to NULL is rejected by the database
Inserting a stock record with inventory_code set to NULL is rejected by the database
Inserting a stock record with quantity set to NULL is rejected by the database
Inserting a stock record with quantity equal to -1 is rejected by the database CHECK constraint at the database layer
Filing a stock level via the API persists a record that is subsequently retrievable with the exact SKU, location, quantity, and inventory_code that were submitted
The stock_records Alembic migration downgrades one step from head and re-upgrades to head without error
Rows seeded into stock_records after the migration upgrade are retrievable with their exact expected field values
Retrieving a previously filed stock record via the API returns the exact quantity and inventory_code that were originally filed
Navigating the stock-retrieve route via <App> renders the stock-record display page
The stock-record display page contains an element carrying data-testid="record-quantity" showing the filed quantity
The stock-record display page contains an element carrying data-testid="record-inventory-code" showing the filed inventory_code
The quantity displayed by data-testid="record-quantity" exactly matches the value that was filed
The inventory_code displayed by data-testid="record-inventory-code" exactly matches the value that was filed
Filing stock for a SKU-location pair that already has a record returns a success response with no error surfaced
After filing stock twice for the same SKU-location pair exactly one record exists for that pair in the store
Filing stock again for an existing SKU-location pair updates the stored record so the retrieved values reflect the second filing rather than the first
The stock service raises a validation error when an upsert write would result in a stock quantity below zero
A second write for the same (sku, location) pair does not create an additional row among the test's own seeded rows
Two concurrent writes for the same (sku, location) pair resolve to exactly one row among the test's own seeded set
A collision upsert does not modify the created_at timestamp of the existing stock record row
Submitting the stock-filing form a second time for the same SKU and location pair does not render any element carrying data-testid="file-error-message"
After a repeat filing for the same SKU and location pair the confirmation element data-testid="file-success-message" is present
Navigating to the retrieve route after a repeat filing via <App> shows the updated quantity from the second filing
